an_air.text: If a hold feels too long, let the breath out early and join the next round.

an_blocked.text: If one side is blocked, don't force it. Lower your hand and breathe normally for a few rounds.

an_bp.text: A few small trials found alternate nostril breathing lowered blood pressure a little. Whether the holds add anything isn't known.

an_close.text: Sit for a moment longer, then open your eyes.

an_hand.text: Bring your right hand up and fold your index and middle fingers down. Your thumb closes the right nostril. Your ring finger closes the left.

an_hold_soft.text: Keep your face and throat soft on the hold, and your fingers light.

an_l_in.text: Thumb on the right. In through the left.

an_l_out_h.text: Release the left, and breathe out.

an_plan.text: We'll warm up with plain alternate nostril breathing. Then we add a hold at the top. The old yoga texts use a ratio of one, four, two: you hold four times as long as you breathe in, and breathe out for twice as long. The counts are a guide. Breathe whenever you need to.

an_r_out_h.text: Release the right, and breathe out.

an_rate.text: Most slow-breathing research is at about six breaths a minute. This is slower, and with holds, so we know less about it.

an_release.text: Release the hand. Breathe through both sides, and let the breath find its own pace.

an_t_arm.text: If your arm gets tired, drop your hand for a few breaths, then pick it back up.

an_t_ears.text: With headphones on, the breath sound follows the side. Left ear, left nostril.

an_t_track.text: Lost track of the side? Breathe in on the side you just breathed out of.

an_t_wander.text: If your mind wanders, use the next switch to come back.

an_welcome.text: Hey. Sit up tall, on a cushion or a chair, and rest your left hand in your lap.

bc_cp_how.text: Test one. Take a small, normal breath in and out through your nose. Then pinch your nose and wait for the first clear urge to breathe. It's not a max hold. The moment the urge comes, let go and tap Breathe now.

bc_ex_how.text: Test two. Take a comfortable full breath in through your nose, then breathe out as slowly as you can without forcing it. Tap Breathe now when you're empty.

bc_gasp.text: If your first breath after that was a gasp, you held on too long. Next time, let go sooner.

bc_log.text: Both times are saved in your log. Check again in a week, at the same time of day. Look for changes over several checks; small differences are normal.

bc_welcome.text: This is a quick check, not a workout. Sit still and breathe normally through your nose for a minute.

bc_why.text: Your hold time varies with sleep, meals, exercise, and how you do the test. One reading tells you little, and it doesn't measure your carbon dioxide level.

bl_asthma.text: Some asthma trials found fewer symptoms and less reliever use after breathing retraining like this. Lung function itself didn't improve.

bl_close.text: Let your breathing go back to normal. If you like, try a minute of lighter breathing at quiet moments during the day.

bl_holds_how.text: Small holds. Breathe out normally and pinch your nose. Let go after a few seconds, or sooner if you need to, and breathe quietly through your nose.

bl_hunger.text: A mild urge for more air is enough. If you're gulping or it feels like a struggle, breathe normally for a bit, then start again.

bl_light_how.text: Now breathe light. Make each breath softer, until you can hardly feel the air at your nostrils. Keep your belly soft.

bl_plan.text: We'll practise breathing a little less air. A few short holds first, then rounds of breathing so light you can barely feel it. You may notice a mild urge for more air, but it should still feel comfortable.

bl_quieter.text: Quieter. If I could hear you, it's too much.

bl_t_shoulders.text: Relax your shoulders, and let your belly move gently as you breathe.

bl_t_small.text: Every hold starts from a normal breath out. Don't empty your lungs.

bl_theory.text: One theory was that this helps by raising carbon dioxide. The trials found benefits without that rise, so nobody knows exactly why it helps.

bl_welcome.text: Sit up, mouth closed, with your tongue resting on the roof of your mouth.

box_check.text: Check how your shoulders, jaw, hands and head feel compared with before. Any change gives you a benchmark.

box_close.text: Practise the drill on calm days so you can use it when things get stressful.

box_empty.text: Before we start, empty out. One long breath through the mouth. <exhales> Good.

box_layers.text: On the way in, fill from the bottom. Belly, then ribs, then chest.

box_lever.text: A long breath out can slow your heart a little. That's why we're lengthening it.

box_plan.text: Here's the plan. Two drills. First, a long breath out, twice as long as the breath in. Then the box: in, hold, out, hold, all the same length. Nothing to win here. Just get the rhythm.

box_plan_none.text: Here's the plan. No holds today. One drill: breathe out twice as long as you breathe in. The long breath out does most of the work.

box_release.text: Let it go. Breathe however you like.

box_soft_hold.text: The holds are a pause, not a squeeze. Throat open, shoulders down.

box_study.text: In a month-long study, five minutes of box breathing a day eased anxiety about as much as the other breathing methods tested. Slowing down may be part of why it helps.

box_t_exact.text: Don't chase the exact count. Just keep all four sides even.

box_throat.text: On the way out, narrow the back of the throat a little, so the air leaves slow and even.

box_welcome.text: Welcome. Sit tall, feet flat on the floor. Close your eyes, or rest them on a spot in front of you.

box_where.text: Police and military teach this one. It's easy to count, and you can do it without anyone noticing.

bs_knees.text: Hands on your knees. Mouth open, and let your breathing do what it needs.

bs_nose.text: When you're ready, in through your nose, and a long, slow breath out through your mouth.

bs_nose_only.text: If it feels easy, close your mouth and breathe slowly through your nose.

bs_why.text: In one small study of soccer players, heart rate came down faster with hands on knees than with hands on head.

cd_check.text: Check your heart rate, breath and head. Notice if anything settled.

cd_close.text: That's the cool-down. Water, food and sleep help you recover from training.

cd_free.text: For the first minute, breathe however you need to. Mouth is fine. Let the panting settle on its own.

cd_low.text: Breathe low. Let the belly rise. The chest can stay quiet.

cd_nose.text: If it feels easy now, close your mouth. Nose in, nose out.

cd_quiet.text: I'll stop talking now. Keep the long breath out, and follow the circle.

cd_return.text: Let go of the count. Breathe on your own.

cd_setup.text: Lie on your back and rest your calves on a chair or a bench, knees and hips bent at right angles. No chair? Just lie flat.

cd_sigh.text: If a big sigh wants to come out, let it. <sighs> That's allowed.

cd_study.text: In a small lab study, slow breathing after cycling brought heart rate down faster than just resting. A bigger trial found no boost to the training itself. So this is for coming down, not for gains.

cd_t_heavy.text: Let the floor take your weight. Heels heavy, hands open.

cd_t_jaw.text: Unclench the jaw. Let the tongue rest.

cd_up.text: Take your legs down, roll onto your side, and get up slowly. Blood pressure can dip after this.

cd_welcome.text: Welcome. You've done the work. Now we bring it down.

cd_why.text: A long breath out can slow your heart a little. It helps your body settle after training.

cl_close.text: Back to quiet breathing through your nose. Come back to this whenever it closes up again.

cl_co2.text: As carbon dioxide builds a little, the nose often opens up for a while. A small study saw the same thing after exercise.

cl_cycle.text: If one side's blocked, that can be normal. Your nose naturally switches sides every few hours. It doesn't necessarily mean your cold's getting worse.

cl_gasp.text: If you gasped on that first breath, you held too long. Let go sooner next time.

cl_how.text: Here's the drill. Small breath in, small breath out. Then pinch your nose and gently nod your head. When you really need to breathe, let go, and breathe in through your nose, gently.

cl_hum_again.text: Three more hums to finish. The sinuses have had time to fill up again.

cl_hum_how.text: We start with three hums. Breathe in through the nose, then hum all the way out with your lips closed.

cl_light.text: Now breathe light. Smaller, quieter breaths than you'd like. A little air hunger, not a lot.

cl_quiet.text: Now just quiet breathing through the nose for a minute. Small and slow.

cl_release.text: Let go. Breathe in through your nose, nice and gentle. No big breath.

cl_silly.text: Yes, you'll look a bit silly. <chuckle> Nobody's watching.

cl_t_first.text: Watch the first breath after the hold. Gentle, through the nose. No gulping.

cl_temp.text: The relief often wears off after a while. That's fine. Do it again later, rather than holding longer now.

cl_welcome.text: Blocked nose? Let's get it open. Sit tall and breathe through your nose, or through whichever side is more open. If it's completely blocked, sip a little air through the corner of your mouth.

hl_calm.text: A minute of easy breathing first. Then the first hold.

hl_close.text: Two or three tables a week is plenty, with a day off in between.

hl_contract.text: If your belly starts to twitch, those are contractions. They're normal. Today, treat them as your signal to stop.

hl_dive.text: Your heart may slow down during the hold, as part of the diving reflex. Every mammal has it.

hl_done.text: That was the last one. Let your breathing settle.

hl_full.text: Every hold starts from a comfortably full breath, not as full as you can get.

hl_last.text: Last hold. Stay soft right to the end.

hl_no_big.text: In the rests, breathe normally. Big or fast breaths before a hold push the urge to breathe back, while your oxygen keeps dropping. That's how people black out.

hl_plan.text: Eight holds, all the same length. The rests get shorter each time, so the urge to breathe tends to come sooner. Your job is to stay relaxed, and to end a hold early whenever you need to.

hl_plan_urge.text: Six holds, no target time. Hold until the first clear urge to breathe, then tap Breathe now. Two minutes of rest between holds. You're learning what a relaxed hold feels like.

hl_recovery.text: Recovery breaths. A quick breath in, a short pause at the top, and let it go.

hl_rest_why.text: Each rest is a bit shorter than the one before, so you start the next hold with more carbon dioxide on board.

hl_rule.text: If you ever feel dizzy or find yourself straining, stop the table there. You can end any hold early.

hl_spleen.text: After a few holds, your spleen can release some extra red blood cells. It's a small effect, and it fades within minutes.

hl_stay.text: Stay sitting or lying for a minute before you get up.

hl_study.text: In one small study, tables like this dropped blood oxygen less than max holds did. Whether they make your max hold longer hasn't been shown.

hl_t_rest_out.text: Let each breath out be a little longer than the breath in.

hl_t_rest_urge.text: Take the whole rest. Start the next hold only when your breathing feels easy again.

hl_t_scan.text: Check for tension, and let go wherever you're still gripping.

hl_t_soft.text: Soften your face. Jaw loose, eyes soft.

hl_t_ten.text: If you need to breathe, breathe. The table will wait.

hl_t_urge.text: Same as before. Breathe at the first clear urge, or sooner if you like.

hl_t_wave.text: Notice the urge when it comes. You can stop there, or stay a little longer if you're still relaxed.

hl_welcome.text: Welcome. This is a breath-hold table, the way freedivers train on dry land. Sit or lie down somewhere you can't fall from. Never do this in water.

kb_air.text: If a hold gets too long, breathe. Join the rhythm again once your breathing feels easy.

kb_close.text: Open your eyes. If the top step stayed easy all the way through, try the next level next time.

kb_co2.text: During the holds, carbon dioxide builds up. That, more than low oxygen, is what makes you want to breathe.

kb_empty_hold.text: The empty hold is usually the harder one. Keep your belly soft, and breathe if you need to.

kb_nose.text: Breathe through your nose the whole time, slow and quiet.

kb_notice.text: Stay here for a minute. See if the breath stays slow on its own.

kb_plan.text: This is kumbhaka: in, hold, out, hold, at a fixed ratio. If you breathe in for four, you hold for eight, breathe out for six, and hold empty for four. We start short and step it up. If you need air before a count ends, just breathe.

kb_rate.text: You're down to under two breaths a minute now. Most slow-breathing research is at about six a minute, so how much of it applies here isn't clear.

kb_release.text: Let go of the count, and breathe at your own pace.

kb_slow_out.text: Let the air out steadily, over the whole count. If you run out early, let it out slower next time.

kb_t_circle.text: You don't have to count. If your eyes are open, the circle keeps time for you.

kb_t_face.text: Let your forehead, your eyes and your jaw go slack.

kb_t_wander.text: If your mind's drifted off, come back on the next breath in.

kb_texts.text: Kumbhaka means the held breath. In the old hatha yoga texts, the holds are the heart of the practice.

kb_top.text: Top step. Same rhythm, longer counts. Stay easy.

kb_welcome.text: Welcome. Sit up tall on a cushion or a chair, hands resting on your knees, and close your eyes.

land_back.text: Start to come back. Wiggle your fingers and your toes.

land_belly.text: Your belly. Let it rise and fall on its own. You don't have to help.

land_chest.text: Your chest and upper back. Notice the breath moving there.

land_close.text: If it's bedtime, you can just stay here. If not, roll onto your side first, and take your time getting up.

land_face.text: Your face. Eyes, forehead, back of your head. Notice any heaviness against the floor.

land_feet.text: Start with your feet. Notice your heels on the floor, your soles and toes. You might feel warmth, cold, tingling, or nothing. That's fine.

land_hands.text: Your hands. Fingertips, palms, the backs of your hands. Then up your arms to your shoulders.

land_hips.text: Now your hips and lower back. Feel where you meet the floor.

land_legs.text: Move up into your calves and knees, then your thighs. Notice whether your legs feel heavy.

land_neck.text: Your neck and jaw. If your jaw feels tense, let it loosen a little.

land_plan.text: We're going to move your attention slowly through your body, from your feet up to your head. Nothing to fix. You don't even have to relax. Just notice what's there.

land_science.text: Body scans are a core part of most mindfulness programs. In trials, those programs help with stress and sleep. The benefits are small, but consistent.

land_sigh.text: Start with one big sigh. In through the nose, and let it all go. <sighs>

land_t_wander.text: If your mind wandered off, that's normal. Pick up wherever you left off.

land_welcome.text: Hey. Lie down on your back, arms by your sides. Palms up, if that feels okay.

land_whole.text: Now the whole body at once, lying here, breathing. Stay with that for a while.

lo_arms.text: Let your arms rest on the bed, and let your hands go loose.

lo_belly.text: Let your belly rise and fall, nice and easy.

lo_close.text: Let the breath go wherever it wants. Goodnight.

lo_face.text: Let your face go slack, from your forehead down to your jaw.

lo_legs.text: Let your legs relax into the bed too.

lo_plan.text: We'll breathe slowly, about six breaths a minute. In through your nose, and out through slightly pursed lips, like cooling a spoonful of soup. I'll talk for the first few minutes, then go quiet.

lo_quiet.text: I'll go quiet now. Just follow the sound of the breath.

lo_rest.text: If sleep doesn't come, that's okay. Lying still and breathing slowly is restful on its own.

lo_shoulders.text: Let your shoulders sink into the bed.

lo_slower.text: The pace slows a little now. Follow it if it feels comfortable.

lo_study.text: In one study, students who did fifteen minutes of this every night for a month rated their sleep better than students who spent that time on their phones.

lo_welcome.text: Hey. Lights off, phone face down. Lie on your back, or however you fall asleep.

n_and_out_as_slowly_as_you_can.text: And out, as slowly as you can.

n_and_pause_up_to_fifteen_seconds_throat.text: And pause, up to fifteen seconds. Throat soft.

n_and_pause_up_to_fifty_seconds_throat_s.text: And pause, up to fifty seconds. Throat soft.

n_and_pause_up_to_forty_seconds_throat_s.text: And pause, up to forty seconds. Throat soft.

n_back_to_four_in_six_out.text: Back to four in, six out.

Breathe in, all the way to the top, and hold. Thirty seconds.

Breathe in, all the way to the top, and hold. Twenty seconds.

n_drill_two_the_box_in_hold_out_hold_fiv.text: Drill two. The box. In, hold, out, hold. Five counts each side.

n_drill_two_the_box_in_hold_out_hold_fou.text: Drill two. The box. In, hold, out, hold. Four counts each side.

n_drill_two_the_box_in_hold_out_hold_thr.text: Drill two. The box. In, hold, out, hold. Three counts each side.

n_five_pauses_growing_from_thirty_second.text: Five pauses, growing from thirty seconds to a minute.

n_five_pauses_of_up_to_fifteen_seconds.text: Five pauses of up to fifteen seconds.

n_four_in_eight_out_five_breaths.text: Four in, eight out. Five breaths.

n_four_in_four_out_we_start_on_the_left.text: Four in, four out. We start on the left.

n_four_in_six_out_six_breaths.text: Four in, six out. Six breaths.

n_hold_eight_of_eight_forty_five_seconds.text: Hold eight of eight. Forty-five seconds.

n_hold_eight_of_eight_one_minute.text: Hold eight of eight. One minute.

Hold, lungs empty, for up to one minute twenty.

n_hold_lungs_empty_for_up_to_thirty_five.text: Hold, lungs empty, for up to thirty-five seconds.

n_hold_lungs_empty_for_up_to_twenty_five.text: Hold, lungs empty, for up to twenty-five seconds.

n_hold_one_of_eight_forty_five_seconds.text: Hold one of eight. Forty-five seconds.

n_hold_one_of_eight_one_minute.text: Hold one of eight. One minute.

n_hold_two_of_eight_one_minute.text: Hold two of eight. One minute.

n_in_for_five_hold_for_twenty_out_for_te.text: In for five, hold for twenty, out for ten. Six rounds.

n_in_for_four_hold_for_sixteen_out_for_e.text: In for four, hold for sixteen, out for eight. Eight rounds.

n_in_for_four_out_for_six_small_and_quie.text: In for four, out for six, small and quiet. About six minutes.

n_in_for_three_hold_for_twelve_out_for_s.text: In for three, hold for twelve, out for six. Six rounds.
In for three, hold for twelve, out for six. Sixteen rounds.

n_in_through_the_nose_for_four_out_throu.text: In through the nose for four, out through the mouth for six. Six breaths.

n_instead_of_pausing_make_the_breath_out.text: Instead of pausing, make the breath out longer. In for four, out for eight.

n_let_s_ease_in_four_in_five_out.text: Let's ease in. Four in, five out.

n_now_cool_down_in_for_four_out_for_eigh.text: Now cool down. In for four, out for eight. Five breaths.

n_now_five_and_a_half_breaths_a_minute_f.text: Now five and a half breaths a minute. Follow the circle.

n_now_five_breaths_a_minute_follow_the_c.text: Now five breaths a minute. Follow the circle.

n_now_five_each_side_same_shape_a_little.text: Now five each side. Same shape, a little longer.

n_now_four_and_a_half_breaths_a_minute_f.text: Now four and a half breaths a minute. Follow the circle.

n_now_four_each_side_same_shape_a_little.text: Now four each side. Same shape, a little longer.

n_now_six_and_a_half_breaths_a_minute_fo.text: Now six and a half breaths a minute. Follow the circle.

n_now_six_breaths_a_minute_follow_the_ci.text: Now six breaths a minute. Follow the circle.

n_now_six_each_side_same_shape_a_little_.text: Now six each side. Same shape, a little longer.

n_now_slow_it_down_in_for_four_out_for_s.text: Now slow it down. In for four, out for six.

n_now_small_slow_breaths_three_in_six_ou.text: Now small, slow breaths. Three in, six out.

n_now_stretch_the_breath_out_four_in_eig.text: Now stretch the breath out. Four in, eight out.

n_pace_five_four_and_a_half_breaths_a_mi.text: Pace five. Four and a half breaths a minute.

n_pace_four_five_breaths_a_minute.text: Pace four. Five breaths a minute.

n_pace_one_six_and_a_half_breaths_a_minu.text: Pace one. Six and a half breaths a minute.

n_pace_three_five_and_a_half_breaths_a_m.text: Pace three. Five and a half breaths a minute.

n_pace_two_six_breaths_a_minute.text: Pace two. Six breaths a minute.

n_pinch_and_nod_let_go_at_the_first_clea.text: Pinch, and nod. Let go at the first clear urge.

n_round_one_five_slow_breaths_then_rest.text: Round one. Five slow breaths, then rest.

n_round_one_small_breath_in_small_breath.text: Round one. Small breath in, small breath out.

n_round_three_five_slow_breaths_then_res.text: Round three. Five slow breaths, then rest.

n_round_two_five_slow_breaths_then_rest.text: Round two. Five slow breaths, then rest.

n_round_two_small_breath_in_small_breath.text: Round two. Small breath in, small breath out. Pinch and nod, until moderate air hunger.

n_slowly_let_your_head_tip_toward_your_r.text: Slowly let your head tip toward your right shoulder.

n_step_one_eight_rounds_four_in_eight_ho.text: Step one. Eight rounds. Four in, eight hold, six out, four hold.

n_step_one_six_rounds_four_in_eight_hold.text: Step one. Six rounds. Four in, eight hold, six out, four hold.

n_step_one_six_rounds_six_in_twelve_hold.text: Step one. Six rounds. Six in, twelve hold, nine out, six hold.

n_step_three_ten_rounds_ten_in_twenty_ho.text: Step three. Ten rounds. Ten in, twenty hold, fifteen out, ten hold.

n_step_three_twelve_rounds_eight_in_sixt.text: Step three. Twelve rounds. Eight in, sixteen hold, twelve out, eight hold.

n_step_two_eight_rounds_eight_in_sixteen.text: Step two. Eight rounds. Eight in, sixteen hold, twelve out, eight hold.

n_step_two_eight_rounds_six_in_twelve_ho.text: Step two. Eight rounds. Six in, twelve hold, nine out, six hold.

n_step_two_eighteen_rounds_six_in_twelve.text: Step two. Eighteen rounds. Six in, twelve hold, nine out, six hold.

n_take_a_break_breathe_normally_for_a_mi.text: Take a break. Breathe normally for a minute.

n_the_box_four_counts_a_side_four_rounds.text: The box. Four counts a side. Four rounds.

rd_blackout.text: One important thing before we start. If you ever twitch, blank out, or lose track of time in a hold, your brain has run short of oxygen. That's not a release. Stop the session there.

rd_close.text: Open your eyes whenever you feel ready.

rd_how.text: Breathe in deep, into your belly and then your chest. Then just let it fall out. Don't push the breath out.

rd_plan.text: Four rounds. Each one starts with a set of full breaths. Then you breathe out and hold with your lungs empty, for as long as it's comfortable. When you need air, take one big breath in and hold it for fifteen seconds. Then a short rest, and we go again.

rd_quiet.text: Let the count go. Rest here for a minute.

rd_study.text: In a month-long study, five minutes a day of fast breathing with short holds lifted mood and eased anxiety. The slower practices did about as well.

rd_t_relax.text: Let your shoulders drop and your hands go soft.

rd_t_rest.text: Breathe normally for a bit, and let yourself settle before the next round.

rd_tap.text: Whenever you need to breathe, tap Breathe now.

rd_tingle.text: You might get tingly hands or a tingly face, or feel a bit lightheaded. That's the fast breathing. If it gets strong, slow down, or just breathe normally.

rd_welcome.text: Hey. Sit or lie down somewhere comfortable, where you can't fall. Never near water with this one.

rd_why.text: Fast breathing lowers carbon dioxide, so the urge to breathe comes later than usual, while oxygen keeps falling. That's why the holds here have a cap.

ready_eyes.text: Keep your eyes on where you're going. Breathe low and quiet.

ready_first.text: Eyes open. Think of the first thing you'll do or say when it starts. Just that one thing.

ready_hum.text: Three hums. Lips closed, teeth apart, and hum at an easy pitch on the way out. It warms up your voice.

ready_low.text: Breathe low, into your belly. Shoulders stay down.

ready_plan_desk.text: Sit tall, feet flat, eyes on one spot. We'll do two sighs, a few long breaths out, then the box.

ready_plan_stage.text: Sit or stand tall, eyes on one spot. Two sighs, a few long breaths out, the box, and three hums to warm up your voice.

ready_plan_start.text: Stand easy, eyes open. Two sighs, then long breaths out. No holds before a start.

ready_sigh.text: Two sighs. Breathe in through your nose, top it up with a second short sniff, then let it all go slowly through your mouth.

ready_why.text: Your heart slows a little each time you breathe out. A few slow breaths can help you settle before you start.

reps_breath.text: Don't change your breathing. Let it do its thing, and just count it.

reps_check.text: Notice how your head feels now, compared to when you sat down. It might be busy, clear, or somewhere in between. Any of that's fine.

reps_close.text: Open your eyes. Go do the first thing on your list.

reps_drift.text: If you just realised you were somewhere else, good. You caught it. Back to one.

reps_lost.text: Got to fifteen? <chuckle> Happens to everyone. Back to one.

reps_plan.text: Here's the drill. Count your breaths out, one to ten, then start again at one. At some point you'll lose count. Everybody does. When you notice, go back to one. Every time you catch it, that's a rep.

reps_t_quiet.text: Keep the count quiet. Like a whisper in your head.

reps_welcome.text: Morning. Sit up, comfortable but awake. Hands on your thighs, and close your eyes.

reps_why.text: Researchers use this exact task, counting breaths to ten, to measure attention. And people get better at it with practice.

res_close.text: Open your eyes when you like. Ten minutes a day is a good start, and more is fine if you enjoy it.

res_find_plan.text: This is a pace test. Five slow paces, two minutes each, with a minute of normal breathing in between. After each one, notice how it felt: smooth and easy, hungry for air, or lightheaded. If a pace makes you lightheaded, stop following it and just breathe.

res_gadget.text: In one study, six breaths a minute raised heart rate variability about as much without a heart monitor as with one. You don't need gadgets for this.

res_light.text: If you feel lightheaded, make the breaths smaller, or stop following the pace for a bit.

res_pick.text: Pick the pace that felt smoothest, without straining or feeling lightheaded. Choose it above the Begin button next time. Test again in a few weeks, because it can shift.

res_plan.text: This is resonance breathing: slow, easy breaths at one steady pace, for about ten minutes. No holds.

res_quiet.text: I'll be quiet for the last few minutes. Stay with the circle.

res_rate.text: How was that one? Smooth, hungry for air, or lightheaded? Remember it.

res_return.text: Let the pace go, and breathe on your own.

res_slower.text: At these slower paces, keep the breaths small and easy.

res_small.text: Slow doesn't mean big. Keep each breath small and smooth.

res_t_nose.text: In and out through your nose, if that feels easy.

res_t_wander.text: If your mind wanders, let the next breath out bring you back.

res_waves.text: At around six breaths a minute, your heart speeds up a little on each breath in and slows on each breath out. Practised regularly, that rhythm is linked with lower stress.

res_welcome.text: Welcome. Sit back, let your hands rest, and close your eyes.

st_close.text: Use this whenever stress has your breathing running ahead of you.

st_plan.text: We'll do ten tiny holds. A small breath out, a short pause, then quiet breathing. If a pause ever feels like too much, skip it and just breathe gently.

st_pull.text: You might feel like taking one big breath. If you can, let that pass. If you're really struggling for air, stop the holds and breathe freely.

st_safety.text: If you have chest pain, or an asthma attack your inhaler isn't helping, stop here and get help instead.

st_small.text: Start each hold after a small, normal breath out. Don't push the air out.

st_t_signs.text: Take your time between holds. Skip the next one if you need to.

st_t_soft.text: Between holds, let your shoulders drop and your belly go soft.

st_welcome.text: Hey. Sit down if you can, and breathe gently through your nose if that's easy.

st_why.text: Breathing fast can lower carbon dioxide and cause dizziness or tingling. Gentler breathing lets it come back up.

tw_checkin.text: Let the breath go. Notice how you feel right now.

tw_close.text: That's it for today. Keep warm, have something hot to drink, and get to bed early. If a fever turns up, skip the rounds and just rest.

tw_co2.text: Quick note. Breathing fast doesn't add much oxygen. Your blood's already nearly full of it. Fast breathing lowers carbon dioxide. That can make you feel tingly or light and make the hold feel easier. The urge to breathe comes mainly from carbon dioxide building back up, not from oxygen running low. That warning can come late. That's why we only do this sitting or lying down.

tw_first.text: Keep the first breath after a hold calm. If you gasped, hold a bit less next time.

tw_gentle.text: Five slow, full breaths through the nose. Then a soft hold, with your lungs empty.

tw_hold_ok.text: Let go at the first strong urge. You can tap Breathe now whenever you want.

tw_hum_again.text: Time for three more hums. The sinuses have had time to fill up again.

tw_hum_how.text: Now some humming. Breathe in through your nose, then hum the whole way out with your lips closed. Keep it low, with your teeth a little apart. You might feel a buzz in your face.

tw_hum_last.text: Three last hums. Long and low.

tw_hum_why.text: Humming vibrates the air in your sinuses, pushing nitric oxide into your nose. One study measured about fifteen times more than during a normal breath out. The first hum releases the most. It takes about three minutes for the sinuses to fill up again, so we use small sets and space them out.

tw_kox.text: In a 2014 study, a group of young men in the Netherlands trained for ten days in a method like this: fast breathing, long holds, cold and meditation. They then got an injection of a toxin that causes flu-like symptoms for a few hours. The trained group had a burst of adrenaline, less inflammation, and felt less sick. But the study was small, they were healthy, and the toxin wasn't a virus. This doesn't cure a cold. It suggests breathing can affect the immune response.

tw_ladder.text: Let's stretch the breath out a little at a time. In for four, out for four. Just follow the circle.

tw_lock.text: Gently lift your pelvic floor and lower your chin a little. Keep it easy, without straining.

tw_lock_short.text: Same lock. Chin down, stay soft.

tw_nh.text: No hold this time. Just breathe easily, and see how you feel.

tw_nose.text: We'll breathe through the nose the whole time. Slow and quiet, no effort.

tw_nose_why.text: Your nose warms and moistens the air, and catches a lot of what's floating around before it reaches your lungs. Your sinuses also make nitric oxide, a gas that helps protect your airways. Mouth breathing skips all of that.

tw_r1.text: Round one. Kapalabhati. Short, sharp breaths out through the nose, from the belly. The breath in happens by itself. Keep your face relaxed.

tw_r2.text: Round two. A few more breaths, and a longer hold. A lot of people find this one easier than the first.

tw_r3.text: Last round. Let it be the easiest one.

tw_r3_after.text: That's three rounds. Your hands and face might feel warm. That's normal.

tw_release.text: Let it go, and breathe normally.

tw_ribs.text: As you breathe in, let your ribs widen out to the sides. Shoulders stay where they are, belly soft.

tw_stay.text: Stay where you are for a minute before you get up. After holds, standing up fast can make you dizzy.

tw_t_ears.text: If you like, rest your thumbs lightly on the little flaps at the front of your ears. The hum may sound louder inside your head.

tw_t_slower.text: If you lose the rhythm, slow down. Keep it steady.

tw_vagus.text: A slow breath out can slow your heart a little. In virus studies, people under a lot of stress caught colds more easily, as did people who slept under six hours a night. So tonight, take it easy and get some sleep. That may help more than this session.

tw_welcome.text: Hey. Rough day? Let's look after you a bit. Sit up tall, or lie down if that's easier, and close your eyes.

ws_brow.text: Let your forehead go smooth. Soften around your eyes, and across your scalp.

ws_checkin.text: Notice how your head and jaw feel now. If something has eased, let it stay that way.

ws_close.text: That's it. Have some water. If the headache keeps going or gets worse, get it checked out. Come back to this whenever you need it.

ws_face_why.text: Your jaw, forehead and shoulders often tighten up around a headache. Letting them go may take off some of the pressure.

ws_h_brow.text: Let your forehead soften, and the muscles around your eyes.

ws_h_hands.text: Let your hands get heavy in your lap.

ws_h_jaw.text: Let your jaw hang soft. Teeth apart.

ws_h_last.text: Last pause. Breathe whenever you like, even before the cue.

ws_h_sway.text: On a train, let it rock you a little instead of bracing.

ws_jaw.text: Lips together, teeth apart. Let your tongue rest on the floor of your mouth.

ws_long_why.text: A longer breath out gives your heart more time to slow down.

ws_neck.text: If it's comfortable, let the back of your neck get long, with your chin tipped down a little.

ws_pain.text: In a lab study, slow breathing with a longer breath out made heat pain a little easier to bear. Whether it helps a headache, nobody knows.

ws_pause_intro.text: Now a few soft pauses. Breathe in to about two-thirds full, then just pause. Throat relaxed, nothing pushing. Let your jaw and shoulders go.

ws_shoulders.text: Every time you breathe out, let your shoulders drop a little more.

ws_silent.text: Everything here is silent. Nose only, small breaths. Nobody around you needs to know.

ws_skip.text: If the throbbing gets worse, or your head feels fuller, skip the pauses for today and just make the breath out longer.

ws_small.text: Slower, not bigger. Big breaths can make you lightheaded.

ws_stress.text: Stress can raise inflammation. If slow breathing helps there, it's probably by lowering stress, and over weeks, not in one session.

ws_t_anchor.text: Keep your attention on the air moving at the tip of your nose.

ws_t_shoulders.text: Check your shoulders again, and let them drop if they've crept up.

ws_t_sounds.text: Let the engine and the voices around you carry on in the background while you follow your breath.

ws_t_wander.text: If your mind wanders off, that's fine. Come back on the next breath out.

ws_t_window.text: If your eyes are open, let them rest on the window. Let the view go by without following it.

ws_vagal.text: Your heart slows a little as you breathe out, partly through the vagus nerve. Whether that does anything for inflammation isn't known.

ws_welcome.text: Hey. Sit back, with your head on the headrest if you can, and your feet flat on the floor. Eyes down, or closed. If you've got water, take a sip now.
